headline: Tecno's new concept phone claims a zero-millimeter bezel, aiming for truly borderless display
summary: Chinese phone maker Tecno is showcasing a concept smartphone at IFA 2026, featuring an 'industry-first' zero-millimeter border. This reengineered display structure aims to eliminate all bezels for an immersive viewing experience.
details: Chinese phone maker Tecno is set to unveil a new concept smartphone at IFA 2026, claiming an 'industry-first' zero-millimeter border. This pushes beyond current flagship phones from Apple, Samsung, Xiaomi, and Honor, which typically achieve 90-95% screen coverage.

The company states this achievement comes from a reengineered display structure, utilizing 'advanced internal stacking' and new screen packing techniques. Tecno specifies the border as 0 microns, effectively eliminating any visible bezel.

While still a concept and not expected until IFA 2026, Tecno highlights an 'immersive viewing experience' free from distracting borders. The press release also mentions 'touch sensitivity', raising questions about potential grip issues on a truly bezel-less device.

Tecno envisions this bezel-less screen forming a 'distinct design language' for its future phones, creating an 'unmistakable identity'. The brand, which rarely launches devices in Western markets, aims to stand out in a consolidating smartphone industry.

headline_marked: [[Sony secures enough RAM]] for all PS5s it expects to sell in fiscal year 2026
headline: Sony secures enough RAM for all PS5s it expects to sell in fiscal year 2026
summary: This assurance comes despite recent sales drops and ahead of the anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 release, which is expected to significantly boost demand for the console.
details: In its latest earnings report, Sony confirmed it has secured the necessary memory to meet its projected PlayStation 5 sales volume for fiscal year 2026, which ends in April 2027. This addresses concerns about potential "Ramageddon" memory shortages impacting console availability.

This assurance is particularly crucial given the anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19th, expected to be a blockbuster title that could significantly boost PS5 demand. Sony did not indicate whether PS5 prices would be increased again over the coming year.

For the first quarter of this fiscal year, Sony sold 1.6 million PS5 consoles, a notable decrease from 2.5 million in the same period last year. The console, now six years old, has shipped 95.3 million units since its June 2020 launch, with recent sales drops attributed to price increases from US tariffs.

Despite the drop in console sales, Sony's profit for the quarter increased by 37 percent to 54.1 billion yen ($337 million), even as overall sales remained flat. This profit surge was primarily driven by US tariff refunds and favorable foreign exchange rates due to the yen's continued depreciation.

Game sales were relatively flat, with third-party sales showing an increase while first-party shipments decreased by 900,000 units, suggesting some PlayStation Studio titles may have underperformed. Meanwhile, PlayStation's monthly active users saw an increase of 2 million, reaching a total of 125 million.
